New Allegations Surface in CINTAA Dispute

Veteran actress Varsha Usgaonkar has raised fresh concerns regarding the administrative and financial operations of the Cine And TV Artists Association (CINTAA). In a recent statement, Usgaonkar alleged that certain staff members are showing favoritism toward prominent committee figures Poonam Dhillon and Padmini Kolhapure, while also failing to provide transparent accounts regarding the organization's finances.

Speaking about her office visits and interactions with association personnel, Usgaonkar emphasized that administrative employees owe their primary loyalty to the organization as a whole rather than to individual committee members. She specifically pointed to the handling of the association's accounts, noting that inquiries regarding fixed deposits (FDs) and organizational funds have allegedly been met with evasive responses from the accounting staff.

Background of the CINTAA Conflict

The ongoing governance dispute within CINTAA originated several months ago when 11 members of the 21-member Executive Committee stepped down, citing concerns over autocratic functioning. The departure led to a widening rift and a series of competing allegations between factions led, on one side, by Padmini Kolhapure and Poonam Dhillon, and on the other, by Upasana Singh and Sahila Chadha.

Previously, Upasana Singh publicly accused Dhillon and Kolhapure of breaking association fixed deposits and transferring funds from a bank account that was reportedly designated to remain frozen during the management dispute. In response to these financial queries, Poonam Dhillon maintained that CINTAA's financial records remain accessible to members of the executive committee.

Legal Developments and Court Intervention

The internal conflict has since moved to the legal arena. According to recent reports, a court has issued a show-cause notice for contempt of court to CINTAA. Furthermore, judicial authorities directed the association not to act upon or implement the results of the October 20 election, an election in which Padmini Kolhapure and Poonam Dhillon had secured the highest number of votes.

Practical Implications and Verification

For members and observers following the situation, the ongoing dispute highlights administrative friction and legal challenges within the prominent industry body.

  • What is Confirmed: Varsha Usgaonkar has publicly criticized CINTAA staff loyalty and questioned the status of organizational fixed deposits. A legal show-cause notice for contempt has been issued, and a court order has directed the association to withhold action on the October 20 election results.
  • What Remains Unknown: The definitive legal status of the disputed financial transactions and the final resolution of the internal management conflict are yet to be determined by the court.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review the original reporting and updates through major entertainment news platforms, including the Times of India Source Report.
